title: The Great Banana Debate
body:
With 32 million shopper notes arguing over banana ripeness, Instacart built a real preference feature in the app, then let social settle the debate. Modeled after the Super Bowl TV spot, the social campaign turned "Team Green" vs. "Team Extra Ripe" into a viral fight across platforms and creator content, culminating in a live debate event hosted by creators Bunch of Friends. All building to a reveal during the big game: "So which banana's best? You decide."

As a result, 249,467 "perfect" bananas were ordered in the first week, plus a Silver Drum and Bronze Clio to round out its success.

title: Community Carts for Los Angeles Fires
awards: One Club Gold Pencil, Campaigns for Good
body:
When the LA wildfires hit in early 2025, Instacart turned "how can we help?" into action. We scaled our Community Carts feature nationwide. Once live, we turned to social to spread the word. We partnered with Kalina Silverman of Make Big Talk to tell real stories from the community — Instacart shoppers shopping the orders, and the businesses and schools receiving them.

As a result of this initiative, 120,000 items were donated from all 50 states. Our good deed didn't go unnoticed, earning us a One Club Gold Pencil for Campaigns for Good.

title: The Lie Pie Kit
body:
Instacart gave hosts a cheeky holiday shortcut by introducing the "Lie Pie," a limited-edition "fake the bake" kit built around a real, perfectly baked pie, and included props like flour to dust the counter, crushed eggshells, pumpkin purée, a pumpkin-scented room spray, and a "well-loved" vintage-style recipe card to provide the illusion of being homemade. In this social-first campaign, we partnered with Boston Rob Mariano, Survivor and Traitors' most legendary strategist, as the perfect face for a campaign built on a lovable lie, along with other creators like Sabrina Brier, Syd Wingold, and Noah Cappe. The campaign drove 7.5M impressions and 26K visits to the landing page.

The Lie Pie ran as an extension of Instacart's broader holiday platform, "Get a Little Magic Delivered," and to top it all off, proceeds from every purchase were donated to Feeding America.

title: We're Here
body:
With cleared IP from a cast of icons like the Kool-Aid Man, the Pillsbury Doughboy, and the Jolly Green Giant, the challenge became finding ways to extend Instacart's Super Bowl commercial well beyond its 30 seconds on air.

So we put the mascots on the road. The Wienermobile — with special mascot guests riding along — delivered real Instacart orders in the Super Bowl host city and in both competing teams' home cities. We also brought the cast to the TODAY show for an in-show feature and appeared as special guests out on the plaza.

All in, the campaign drove more than 1,200 placements and 12 billion earned impressions.
